JSON: Name: operando_pd_acetate_speciation_pipeline Title: An operando spectro-crystallographic and computational workflow to map Pd-acetate trimer/dimer dynamics and correlate speciation with vinyl acetate monomer selectivity in silica-supported heterogeneous catalysts Short Hypothesis: If ≥25% of surface Pd is present as KnPd2(OAc)n+4 during steady-state vapor-phase vinyl acetate monomer (VAM) synthesis, then the average Pd nanoparticle diameter will be <3.5 nm and the VAM formation rate will be ≥10× the rate measured when ≤5% of surface Pd is present as KnPd2(OAc)n+4 under identical reaction conditions. Related Work: Prior studies have applied individual operando probes (DRIFTS, XAS, operando XRD, TEM) and DFT to investigate heterogeneous VAM catalysts and have reported correlations between alkali promotion, Pd-acetate molecular species, nanoparticle size, and activity. Homogeneous Pd-acetate chemistry shows that Pd-acetate trimers/dimers engage in redox and ligand exchange cycles that enable olefin acetoxylation. Existing heterogeneous work establishes that KOAc promotion correlates with increased VAM rates and distinct νas(COO) features attributed to Pd-acetates, but limitations remain: single-technique studies cannot quantify transient speciation or resolve whether molecular Pd-acetates are active complexes or reservoirs; spectroscopy suffers from overlapping vibrational bands and unknown extinction coefficients; ex situ TEM/XRD/XAS cannot capture early-time redox dynamics; and computational studies often treat only thermodynamics without direct operando validation. These gaps prevent causal linkage between Pd-acetate speciation, nanoparticle formation pathways, and catalytic metrics. Abstract: We propose an integrated operando spectro-crystallographic and computational workflow to quantify Pd-acetate trimer and dimer speciation dynamics and directly correlate those dynamics with nanoparticle formation and catalytic performance during vapor-phase vinyl acetate monomer (VAM) synthesis on silica-supported Pd catalysts. The workflow combines time-resolved DRIFTS peak deconvolution and calibrated integrated intensities, operando XRD grain analysis, in situ Pd K-edge XAS EXAFS coordination fitting, ex situ HAADF-STEM/EDS particle mapping, and DFT thermodynamic calculations to compute reaction free energies for trimer↔dimer↔KnPd2(OAc)n+4 transformations. The primary contribution is a standardized experimental–computational pipeline that yields quantitative speciation fractions, nanoparticle size distributions, and thermodynamic predictions under identical reaction conditions, enabling direct statistical tests of causal relationships between promoter-driven molecular species and VAM rate/selectivity. Expected outcomes include validated thresholds for promoter-induced dimer persistence associated with reduced Pd clustering, a mechanistic redox map of Pd-acetate transformations, and a set of spectroscopic/speciation markers predictive of catalyst activity and selectivity for catalyst design and screening. Experiments: Datasets: prepare and test catalysts: (A) PdOAc/SiO2 (6 wt% Pd, no K), (B) PdOAc/KOAc/SiO2 (6 wt% Pd, 0–5 wt% K series: 0,1,3,5 wt% K), (C) PdAu/SiO2 and PdAu/KOAc/SiO2 conventional benchmarks (8 wt% Pd, 4 wt% Au, 0–3 wt% K), and (D) homogeneous Pd(OAc)2 solution control. Reaction conditions (all operando measurements): 150°C, 1 atm, 50 sccm total flow, gas composition 15 vol% C2H4 / 5 vol% AcOH / 2 vol% O2 (balance He), time-on-stream 0–180 min; replicate n=3 per condition. Operando measurements: continuous DRIFTS (2000–1100 cm−1, 128 scans, 4 cm−1 resolution) with calibrated standards (Pd3(OAc)6, Pd(OAc)2, KOAc) to obtain integrated νas(COO) peak areas; operando XRD (2θ 30–70°, 0.005° step) for (111) peak deconvolution and Scherrer grain-size analysis; time-resolved Pd K-edge XAS (XANES+EXAFS) for Pd oxidation state, Pd-Pd coordination number, and Pd-O coordination fraction; online GC (FID+TCD) for product quantification (VAM, CO2, others) to compute VAM formation rate (μmol g−1 min−1) and selectivity; ex situ HAADF-STEM/EDS for particle size distribution (measure ≥300 particles) and Pd/C mapping; XRD lattice parameter extraction for PdCx fraction. Baselines: KOAc-free PdOAc/SiO2, PdAu/SiO2; additional baseline: pre-reduced PdO/SiO2. Evaluation metrics: VAM formation rate (μmol g−1 min−1), selectivity to VAM (% carbon), average Pd particle diameter (nm), Pd-Pd EXAFS coordination number (N Pd-Pd), fraction of Pd as Pd-O (Pd2+ organic fraction %), integrated DRIFTS-species fractions (relative % of peaks assigned to Pd3(OAc)6, Pd2(OAc)4, KnPd2(OAc)n+4, KOAc), PdCx fraction from XRD (% of Pd-containing phase). Comparisons and ablation studies: (1) KOAc loading series to correlate KnPd fraction vs particle size and VAM metrics; (2) water-content ablation: dry feed vs 1000 ppm H2O to test trimer dissociation effect; (3) time-resolved vs steady-state comparison: analyze 0–30 min vs 30–180 min intervals; (4) DFT ablation: compute ΔG for transformations with and without explicit KOAc inclusion and compare predicted equilibrium speciation to operando DRIFTS/XAS quantification. Analysis: compute Pearson and Spearman correlations between KnPd fraction and particle size, VAM rate, and selectivity; perform ANOVA across KOAc loadings (α=0.05) and report mean±s.d.; perform regression to test threshold hypothesis (≥25% KnPd vs ≤5% KnPd). Calibration: determine relative extinction factors for key νas(COO) bands using prepared standard mixtures; estimate uncertainty propagation for speciation fractions. Risk Factors and Limitations: Spectroscopic quantification errors: overlapping DRIFTS peaks and unknown or variable extinction coefficients may bias speciation fractions; calibration against powdered standards may not perfectly mimic supported environments. Beam-induced alteration: prolonged XAS/XRD exposure may reduce Pd-acetate species or cause nanoparticle sintering, altering in situ speciation. Temporal resolution: fast redox/transformation kinetics (<seconds) may be under-sampled by instrument duty cycles, missing transient intermediates. Spatial heterogeneity: operando bulk probes average over particle populations and may not capture local site heterogeneity; TEM sampling is ex situ and may not represent in situ distributions. DFT limitations: approximate functionals and finite models may misestimate ΔG for PdCx and charged complexes, and entropic/solvation corrections for gas–surface equilibria are approximate. Generalization: results obtained on silica-supported, physically mixed Pd-acetate model catalysts and KOAc promoters may not transfer to industrial PdAu alloy formulations, different supports, or scaled reactors. Compute and access constraints: time-resolved XAS/XRD beamtime and high-level DFT on large cluster models are resource intensive and may limit parameter sweeps. Experimental reproducibility: sensitivity to residual water, handling, and sample preparation may introduce variability across replicates.
